newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's February trade deficit seen up 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's February trade deficit seen up 40 pct.

text.p: Preliminary and long-delayed trade data showed that Turkey's trade deficit in February migh thave risen by some 40 percent over the same 1995 month to around $1 billion, a goverment official said on Wednesday.
According to preliminary figures, exports stood at $1.7 billion and imports at $2.6 in February, compared with February 1995 figures of 1.55 billion and 2.28 billion, respectively.
Turkey's January exports were $1.73 billion and imports $3.02 billion. The government had set its 1996 target at $25 billion for exports and $41 billion for imports.
Economists expect the 1996 deficit to exceed the target.
"February figures will be finalised and announced officially in coming days," the official told Reuters.
Technical problems at customs, caused by Turkey's customs union with the European Union, have delayed the announcement of trade figures. -- Ankara newsroom +90-312-446 2940
